newsitem.title: USA: Carter sets Africa visit for late August.
newsitem.headline: Carter sets Africa visit for late August.

text.p: Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter will visit Ethiopia, Mali and Mozambique this month to discuss food and economic development in Africa, the Carter Center said on Monday.
Carter will visit Ethiopia Aug. 23-27, where he will meet with Prime Minister Meles Zenawi and officials from 14 African countries at a conference on food production in sub-Saharan Africa.
"The global community needs to move forward in helping these nations invest in infrastructure, agricultural research and development, and financial markets," the former president said in a statement.
"Without these core elements, sub-Saharan Africa will not be able to feed its people," he added.

Carter also was scheduled to meet with Mozambique President Joaquim Alberto Chissano and Mali President Oumar Konare to discuss efforts to organize governmental and international donor agency support for economic and social development in emerging democracies on the continent.
